title: QUIC RFC 9000 S13 Periodic ACK-Probe Scheduling
purpose: Describe the focused ACK deadlock avoidance floor that sends periodic ack-eliciting PING probes when recovery has no retransmittable payload to send, while keeping the short application-send delay bounded.
design_summary: The active-path send policy can briefly queue small application stream writes so adjacent frames can be packed into a single 1-RTT packet, but the boundary does not hold packets at or above the configured small-packet threshold. Separately, the recovery PTO fallback emits a PING frame, not PADDING-only data, when the selected Application Data space has no retransmittable payload or queued application send available. That PING probe is ack-eliciting, non-ACK-only, non-retransmittable, and marked as a probe packet so later PTO expirations can emit another PING rather than trying to retransmit the previous probe.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice reuses the existing recovery controller, active-path packet protection, timer recomputation, and sender packet tracking state. PING probe packets are tracked in Application Data packet-number space as ack-eliciting probes while remaining non-retransmittable. The short application-send delay remains bounded by the existing 32-byte threshold and 1000 microsecond delay policy.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A small stream write can wait for the short application-send delay so a nearby write or FIN can be packed into the same packet.
A stream write at the delay threshold sends immediately and does not arm the application-send delay timer.
The periodic recovery probe carries PING as the first non-PADDING frame.
The PING probe path is unavailable without an active path and 1-RTT packet protection material.
The PING probe is not treated as retransmittable payload, allowing a later PTO to send another periodic probe.
risks: This slice proves a bounded active-path Application Data deadlock-avoidance floor, not a complete pacing or packet-batching scheduler.
This slice does not claim candidate-path or multipath packet scheduling.
This slice does not claim endpoint interop success beyond the traced S13 requirement homes.
This slice does not alter public APIs.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the focused S13 periodic ACK-probe scheduling gap for RFC9000-S13-P2-S2-R01 and RFC9000-S13-2-7-P1-S3-R01 only. It keeps broader packet-composition completeness, PMTU behavior, candidate-path scheduling, and hosted interop readiness out of scope.
